summary: Persistent silent tail on extended max_tokens causing client heartbeat failures and 504s
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using large max_tokens (>= 120k) combined with multi-part system prompts report long periods of silence near the end of generation followed by client-side 504s or aborted websocket connections. The silence is observed even though the model is still producing tokens on the server side (server metrics show GPU utilization and token emission spikes), suggesting an intermittent stall in the streaming path.

Impact:
- Affected NimbusAI production workloads (dedicated cluster) experiencing ~20-40% of long-run requests terminating with 504 or websocket reconnects.
- Customer reports timeouts on batches used for document synthesis; user-facing features degrade.

Environment:
- prod (us-east-1), dedicated capacity (cluster: nimbus-prod-3)
- Models: redwood-13b-v2 and quantized mistral-7b used in different routes
- Request pattern: large system prompt (~80k tokens) + max_tokens=130000, streaming enabled, heartbeat pings every 15s from client

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a streaming completion request with a large system prompt that primes multi-hop context (>70k tokens).
2) Set max_tokens to >100k and client heartbeat interval 15s.
3) Observe initial token emission for minutes, then a 20-60s silent window where no chunks arrive to client, followed by either a 504 or client-triggered reconnect.

Observed behavior:
- Server-side logs show continued finalizer queue entries and occasional token emission traces, but websocket stream sinks at the API gateway show no forwarded chunks during the silence window.
- KV-cache activity shows bursts of serialization and then a pause correlated with the silent period.
- API gateway reports large write latencies to upstream during the windows.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous streaming of chunks to client until generation finishes or explicit server-side error is returned. Short pauses (<5s) are acceptable; long silent windows should not happen.

Preliminary hypothesis:
- A blocked async writer at the gateway or backpressure miscalculation during extreme prefix handling causes intermittent stalls.
- KV-cache serialization spikes (large prefix snapshots) may be contending with network flushes, causing the streaming pipeline to starve the websocket forwarding loop.

Mitigation / Workaround applied to customer:
- Recommended reducing max_tokens to <= 60k and splitting the generation into incremental calls. This reduced incident rate to <5% for their workload.
- Increased client heartbeat timeout to 90s as a temporary measure.

Next steps:
- SRE/serving-runtime to replicate in staging with synthetic 100k+ prefix tests.
- Investigate API gateway write buffer behavior under prolonged streaming and KV snapshot activity.
- Add extra tracing for websocket forwarder and finalizer handoff.
- Consider prioritizing streaming flushes over KV-cache checkpointing when active stream is detected.
comments: Maya Patel (Support) - 2026-03-12: Customer reported repeated 504s during long completions. Collected request IDs and initial logs; reproduced silence locally with a trimmed prompt. Escalating to SRE since this looks infrastructural.

Ethan Brooks (SRE) - 2026-03-13: Dug into gateway logs for request-id SUP-772210-req1. Found repeated ECONNRESET on the upstream write path coincident with KV-cache flushes. Spinning up staging test to reproduce at scale.

Ava Chen (Customer) - 2026-03-13: We applied the suggested max_tokens reduction; errors dropped significantly. Still need long-run support for document synthesis use cases. Asking for ETA on permanent fix or mitigation in platform.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13: Reproduced in staging using synthetic prefix generator (script attached to GH PR). Observed write stalls in gateway process PID 8142 that line up with large KV snapshot durations.
2026-03-13: Heap and FD counts on gateway increased during test; suspect epoll loop stalls under large buffered writes and blocking fsync during snapshot write.
2026-03-14: Temporary experiment: throttling KV checkpoint frequency in staging eliminated the silent tail in 10/10 runs. Need safe rollout plan.
resolution: Mitigation suggested (reduce max_tokens, increase heartbeat timeout). Working on a gated change to defer KV-cache full checkpoints when active streaming is detected. No permanent fix yet; ETA for gated rollout: 2026-03-21.
